rows.Purpose / validation rule: Stable linkage to question, option definitions and evaluation set; changes require versioning.
Define exactly one candidate, evidence item or comparison; do not mix unrelated entities in a state.
Fix the biological question and target setting before asking about applicability.
Only include context that can change the answer. Missing fields remain null/unknown.
Supply computed effects, units, uncertainty and QC; never ask the model to calculate these.

rows.Who supplies it: Scripts; cached LLM extraction if needed
rows.Example: SYNTHETIC E1: Recovery was assessed after adding recombinant A to buffer.
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Prefer a short original methods/result passage to an LLM interpretation. Keep qualifications and negative results.
Retain a source URL/DOI/accession plus page/section/row/span. Input provenance is not proof of what the model relied on.
Do not silently convert an author's mechanistic interpretation into an observed result.

rows.Example: observed | not_measured | not_reported | inaccessible | extraction_failed | truncated
rows.Purpose / validation rule: A null result differs from an unmeasured endpoint, a nondetect and missing text.
Needed for evidence-gap questions; never translate incomplete retrieval into literature-wide novelty.
Track algorithm, model/checkpoint, prompt, source and data versions for reproducibility.
Use numerical summaries or validated descriptions. No direct pixel, FCS-event or raw spectral reading by Jev/Laya is assumed.
For panel/region comparisons, all parallel questions use the same fixed reference set. Update between rounds, not within a batch.

rows.Example: Use only supplied evidence; choose one option; abstain when decisive facts are missing.
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Include source-as-data handling and the mixed/conflict versus missing-evidence distinction described in Start_here.
Conceptual specification: map to the installed Jev/Laya API. No assumption that their outputs or confidence fields are identical.

rows.Example: Does the cited assay-validation experiment support use in the proposed specimen matrix?
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Ask one bounded question. Do not include the expected label, downstream decision or an upstream LLM verdict.

rows.Example: A: Direct matrix evidence; B: Related matrix requiring validation; C: Different matrix only; D: Conflicting evidence; U: Insufficient evidence
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Use concise, distinguishable options with stable keys; test paraphrases and option order.
Log an actual model output only after execution. No model predictions are supplied in this workbook.

rows.Example: Not populated — the proposed questions have not been run.
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Check schema, bounds and normalization as applicable; preserve the raw distribution before any calibration.
Keep distinct from maximum class probability and from task-specific calibrated correctness.
Do not attach a universal 0.8/0.9 threshold or assume vendor-reported calibration transfers.
These are input provenance links. They are not automatically model-selected citations or an explanation.
Apply expert-approved rules to independent answers; do not multiply correlated probabilities as independent evidence.
Final interpretation, experimental design, clinical decisions and diagnostic gating remain with qualified humans.

rows.Example: Not populated — measure during the pilot.
rows.Purpose / validation rule: Count actual model input including questions/options. Record retrieval, extraction, GPU/CPU, model calls and expert time.

rows.Proposed test: Define the intended use, unit, options, mixed/conflicting precedence and missing-evidence policy with domain experts.
rows.What to measure: Inter-rater agreement; disagreements requiring revised definitions.
rows.Failure to prevent: No downstream model result available to labelers.

rows.Proposed test: Compare the proposed layer against existing rules, ontology matching, specialist software and a compact supervised classifier where appropriate.
rows.Failure to prevent: Remove questions already solved by structured fields from the Jev/Laya workload.

rows.Proposed test: Compare original retrieved spans with cached LLM-extracted facts, holding the question and candidate set fixed.
rows.What to measure: Extraction errors; missing decisive facts; decision accuracy; preparation cost.
rows.Failure to prevent: Do not give Jev/Laya an upstream LLM answer to the same question.

rows.Proposed test: Use independently labeled real task cases, with expert adjudication; retain difficult and rare categories.
rows.What to measure: Agreement; class support; adjudicated error types.
rows.Failure to prevent: LLM-generated labels may assist training but are not an independent gold standard.

rows.Proposed test: Split at the biological/source dependence unit: patient, family, donor, slide, study or locus as applicable.
rows.What to measure: Performance on unseen sources, cohorts and institutions.
rows.Failure to prevent: Keep reused excerpts, candidate-panel relatives and duplicate experiments in one split.

rows.Proposed test: Evaluate pinned Jev and Laya versions separately. Fit any task adaptation and calibration only on development/calibration data.
rows.What to measure: Macro-F1; class recall; Brier score; reliability plots; calibration by question/domain.
rows.Failure to prevent: Keep a final held-out test set. Laya's model card warns about zero-shot limits and overconfidence; no biomedical transfer is assumed.

rows.Proposed test: Choose routing thresholds from the accepted error rate for each task, not an arbitrary global confidence cut-off.
rows.What to measure: Risk–coverage curve; retained-candidate recall; review workload.
rows.Failure to prevent: Always route missing context and out-of-domain inputs independently of reported confidence.

rows.Proposed test: Audit retrieved methods/results, entity identity, supplementary data, negative results and source access.
rows.What to measure: Recall of decisive evidence; source-link accuracy; unsupported extraction rate.
rows.Failure to prevent: Do not score missing retrieved evidence as a biological negative or proof of novelty.

rows.Proposed test: Change one relevant fact: specimen, transcript, comparator, temporal anchor, marker condition or assay format.
rows.What to measure: Expected label-change rate and irrelevant-change stability.
rows.Failure to prevent: Synthetic tests check sensitivity, not real-world biomedical performance.

rows.Proposed test: Vary option order and equivalent wording; test mixed, contradictory and insufficient cases.
rows.What to measure: Label/probability stability and systematic option bias.
rows.Failure to prevent: Short option sets must still be distinguishable; inspect tokenized input, not just character count.

rows.Proposed test: Compare scripts → LLM/expert with scripts → decision layer → LLM/expert using the same retrieved evidence and final review budget.
rows.What to measure: Relevant candidates retained; time to review; end-to-end errors and costs.
rows.Failure to prevent: An accurate local classifier can still harm the workflow by filtering out useful candidates.

rows.Proposed test: Sample retained, lowered-priority, bypassed and abstained cases; deliberately inspect rare/poorly annotated candidates.
rows.What to measure: False-negative candidate rate; rare-class recall; under-annotation bias.
rows.Failure to prevent: Preserve a contradiction and discovery queue. No blanket exclusion for insufficient evidence.

rows.Proposed test: Evaluate descriptor generation and semantic decision separately, then together against image/spectrum-grounded expert labels.
rows.What to measure: Upstream-versus-decision error attribution; rare-lesion or isomer loss.
rows.Failure to prevent: Never claim direct Jev/Laya image/spectral understanding from results on prepared text.

rows.Proposed test: Measure preprocessing, retrieval, extraction, decision calls, downstream LLM calls, review and cache reuse under the actual workload.
rows.What to measure: Total cost per retained useful candidate; amortized extraction cost; latency percentiles.
rows.Failure to prevent: Scripts and self-hosted models have compute/storage/maintenance costs; there is no zero-cost assumption.

rows.Proposed test: Validate the biological target: held-out protein-panel performance, perturbation, analytical identity, gate membership or pathology interpretation.
rows.Failure to prevent: Semantic-label agreement alone is not a discovery, biomarker validation or clinical validation.

rows.Proposed test: Version sources, definitions, checkpoints and rules; minimize personal data; obtain approvals appropriate to data and intended use.
rows.What to measure: Traceability; access controls; audit completeness; dataset/model drift.
rows.Failure to prevent: Use research routing only until the applicable clinical and institutional validation requirements are met.

rows.What this source supports: Typed questions over a shared state; separate atomic decisions and combine them in code.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Describes the interface/design pattern, not biomedical validation.

rows.What this source supports: Choice questions, criteria and structured choice outputs.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Check the current API schema when implementing an adapter.
Provider confidence is not automatically a calibrated probability of biomedical correctness.

rows.What this source supports: Text/JSON state, typed decisions, checkpoint/token-budget differences; warns about zero-shot performance and calibration.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Developer-reported benchmarks are not validation of these biomedical questions. Pin checkpoint and runtime versions.

rows.What this source supports: Count-based differential-expression analysis as an upstream statistical task.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Differential expression alone does not establish causality, protein abundance or biomarker performance.

rows.What this source supports: Programmatic retrieval of pathway records and biological annotations.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Annotations are evidence inputs; absence of an annotation is not evidence of irrelevance.

rows.What this source supports: Variant consequences, reference annotations and population frequencies can be computed/retrieved upstream.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Predicted molecular consequence is not equivalent to disease causation.

rows.What this source supports: Current portal for aggregated, mechanism- and evidence-specific variant-classification recommendations.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Research triage does not replace professional variant classification or the applicable evidence framework.

rows.What this source supports: Automated cell-type annotation and prediction outputs as upstream inputs.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Do not replace a trained classifier with marker-name intuition; assess discordant cases.

rows.What this source supports: Registry of candidate cis-regulatory elements derived from ENCODE data.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Candidate-element annotation alone does not prove a target gene or regulatory mechanism.

rows.What this source supports: Specialist mass-spectrometry tools produce molecular-formula, structure-candidate and chemical-class annotations.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Contextual plausibility must not override analytical evidence or identify unresolved isomers.

rows.What this source supports: Profiling microbial molecular functions and metabolic pathways from sequencing data.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Functional potential and measured metabolite production are different evidence types.

rows.What this source supports: Rule-based negation, experiencer and temporality extraction; baseline for short clinical-text processing.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Use semantic triage only for unresolved contextual cases, not as a replacement for simple reliable rules.
Gate geometry, compensation and numerical quality checks remain upstream.

rows.What this source supports: Digital-pathology image analysis provides regions, objects and measurements.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: The proposed decision layer consumes descriptors; direct slide-image input is not assumed.

rows.What this source supports: Programmatic discovery of reusable open-access article resources.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Availability and permitted reuse depend on the article/license. Retrieval coverage must be recorded.

rows.Source: Uhlen et al. — A proposal for validation of antibodies (2016)
rows.What this source supports: Antibody validation is application- and context-specific; identity and experimental validation should be documented.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Supports examining validation scope, not ranking a particular antibody or validating a Jev/Laya task.

rows.What this source supports: Statistical analysis of mass-spectrometry-based protein quantification as an upstream task.
rows.Limitation / use in this workbook: Quantification and statistical testing remain in specialist software, not the semantic decision model.
